# goncordia

> Transactional job queue engine for Go with ten storage backends, typed futures, crash recovery, pipeline serialization, leader-safe schedules, an embeddable admin UI, OpenTelemetry, and deterministic injected clocks.

## Key concept

`EnqueueTx` enqueues a job inside your existing database transaction. The job becomes visible to workers only if the transaction commits — no dual-write risk, no relay process needed.

```go
tx, _ := pool.Begin(ctx)
queries.CreateOrder(ctx, tx, order)
client.EnqueueTx(ctx, tx, SendConfirmationArgs{OrderID: order.ID}, nil)
tx.Commit(ctx)  // job and order appear atomically
```

## Futures

`future.Enqueue` returns a `Future[R]`; `Await` returns the value produced by a `future.RegisterWorker` handler. Works on every backend; in-process waiters wake instantly, others poll.

```go
m, _ := future.New(d, future.Config{})
future.RegisterWorker(registry, m, func(ctx context.Context, job *core.Job[SumArgs]) (int, error) { return job.Args.A + job.Args.B, nil }, core.WorkerOpts{})
f, _ := future.Enqueue[int](ctx, m, client, SumArgs{A: 2, B: 3}, nil)
sum, err := f.Await(ctx)
```

## Supported backends

Postgres (pgx v5, database/sql, gorm, bun), MySQL, SQLite, MongoDB, Redis, Cassandra, ClickHouse, Amazon DynamoDB, Cloud Firestore, in-memory.

Transactional inserts supported on: Postgres, MySQL, SQLite, MongoDB, Firestore, in-memory.
